gates.text: The receiving session owns the run, not a delegated replacement coordinator. Select and fully read the matching native playbook, then open a task checklist whose FIRST items copy that playbook’s native steps VERBATIM, before task-specific items. Retain every skipped step with `skip: <one-line reason>`; a required gate that cannot run is BLOCKED, not an optional skip. Large/cross-cutting work, work the user will review later, or no fitting playbook uses figure-it-out; a genuine standing multi-day program uses orchestrate, while one-session work follows its collapse rule.

Apply the actual triggers, not a generic three-step substitute: nontrivial change, architecture decision or “are we sure?” → how; an empirical approach fork → authorized prototype/measurement rather than asking the human for an observable fact (read-only investigation stays read-only); code → name its data shape and read principle-model-the-domain; crossing function boundaries → architect before implementation; partitioned/race fan-out → swarm, whole-artifact bakeoff → arena; contested design → interrogate before shipping; nontrivial multi-step work → the matching throughput checkpoint. Only a genuinely missing product/preference/safety choice goes to the user. Authorization and explicit named gates still win.

Any prose including replies → unslop; docs/RFCs/README/PR descriptions/commit messages → technical-writing; skill authoring → installed native skill-creator. Before commit, discover an applicable native cleanup/review skill rather than importing Cursor deslop; before review → no-comments under its real scope and required gates. For UI/IDE/CLI changes use the matching installed native control skill and reproduce a bug on that surface. Before acting on a measured number → benchmark-checklist. PR-status work → babysit with a declared mode, never implicitly from opening a PR; authorized landing → shipping’s contiguous verified run. Assess automated review comments skeptically against concrete evidence, not automatic agreement or dismissal.

Read the FULL applicable leaf section in native principles.md before applying it, including principles for domain/architecture, reader load, root causes, real behavioral verification, verifiable units and explaining measured numbers. In the reply name EACH principle that shaped a decision and the specific choice it changed, with a resolving source pointer. Cite only principles actually read this session, not a decorative catalog. Ground in source, state the observable done predicate and authorized scope, and verify each bounded unit against the real artifact.

Use native role routing and delegation, never upstream Task/custom-agent registration, Cursor paths, orchestration/log scripts or guessed model-slug fallbacks. EVERY required independent phase MUST resolve pstack_route, use emitted arguments with native sessions_spawn and collect through its accepted completion path, or name that gate BLOCKED; even a matching-model sequential parent pass cannot satisfy independence. Preserve existing owners, snapshots and explicit corrections; children already executing an assigned role do not recursively redispatch it. Inspect all artifacts/diffs and own the final synthesis rather than forwarding self-reports.

Long/autonomous/multi-phase work or a user stepping away requires native show-me-your-work with its audit/review gates; a broken skill is an explicit repair/blocker through its canonical owner, not a silent workaround or automatic unrelated PR. Autonomy does not authorize external/destructive actions, provider changes, jobs, publication or bypassing explicit pauses. Keep comments for non-obvious why/real constraints under no-comments’ safe adaptation. Finish with consumer/maintainer impact, actual results/evidence, tradeoffs/open decisions and unresolved gates in plain prose; never fabricate links. Future route commands use `pstack-<route>`; bare names are explicit opt-in only and never shadow core. The native/requirements JSON guards are text regression only, not behavioral proof.

For long routed phases, spawn announcing children (without `collect`; a collector is collected in the turn that spawned it) and use a short schema-supported bounded native wait, then hand off the exact owner, accepted run/session IDs, phase, routing snapshot, completed artifacts and next collection action in the task-owned record, and finish on resume under [the shared lifecycle](contract.md#collection-and-resume). Never respawn accepted children, synthesize before required results arrive or call pending work complete. Unattended continuation runs only for native controller workflows (/pstack-architect, -arena, -interrogate, -swarm, -how, -why, -reflect) on hosts that grant requester-admitted scheduled command turns; otherwise that gate is BLOCKED when requested, with an explicit resume handoff, not an ad-hoc scheduler.

7. Render each helper or code-writing delegate with `pstack_brief` profile `poteto-agent` and check its returned `delegate-result` with `pstack_brief` before inspecting its diff; see [native agent briefs](agent-briefs.md). A delegate that skipped a required native read or reports PASS over a failing check is rejected, not summarized.

8. Every claim carries its evidence or its label in the same sentence: measured, inferred or guess. A prediction or an unseen cause is a guess. Run a check you can run yourself instead of handing it to the human; name the missing capability for one you cannot run.

9. Deliver a routed explainer, judgment or prose result verbatim, quoted and attributed under [delivering a routed result](delegation.md#delivering-a-routed-result). A parent conclusion that differs from the child's goes outside the quote, labelled as the parent's, with its own evidence; it never silently replaces the child's conclusion.

10. Plan every required phase under the [planner call](delegation.md#planner-call): the how explainer or explorers a trigger requires, `judgment and prose` for the reply whenever its selection differs from or cannot be verified against the parent, and each `poteto-agent` delegate. Spawn each with its returned arguments and collect it, or name that phase BLOCKED. A phase planned without `spawnSchema`, or planned and never spawned, is not routed. Check each delegate's `delegate-result` with `pstack_brief` before summarizing its report; an unchecked report is named unvalidated, not summarized as findings.

11. When `pstack_brief` rejects a routed explainer's or delegate's report, rerun it once as a fresh child: plan the same role again under the [planner call](delegation.md#planner-call), add the check's exact errors to the task, spawn it and check the new report. A collector child is one-shot, so a refused `sessions_send` does not end the phase. Only a second rejection leaves that phase BLOCKED, and the parent's own probe never stands in for it.

12. Show the opened checklist in the reply: the matching playbook's native steps copied verbatim as its first items, then the task items. Before handback, mark every item done, `skip: <reason>` or BLOCKED; an unmarked item fails this gate.

13. Before sending the reply, check every sentence that makes a claim: it carries its evidence or the word measured, inferred or guess. For code work the reply names the data shape it chose, such as the event type a trigger receives, and each principle that shaped a decision.
